    72	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    73	  [Algebra k R]
    74	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
    75	
    76	/-! ## Certified families over a widened cover -/
    77	
    78	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
    79	system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
    80	the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
    81	`FinCoverData`. -/
    82	structure CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff (n : ℕ) : Type u where
    83	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
    84	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
    85	  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/
    86	  cover : AffCoverData C R
    87	  /-- The adaptation of the system to that cover. -/
    88	  adaptation : AffAdaptation cover eqns
    89	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
    90	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
    91	
    92	/-! ## The widened locally-certified predicate -/
    93	
    94	variable {C R}
    95	
    96	/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
    97	(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over
    98	the away localizations, divisor-equal to the pulled system — except that the local
    99	certificates live over ARBITRARY AFFINE-OPEN covers.
   100	
   101	The base-side structure is untouched on purpose: R2 widens where the pieces live on the
   102	CURVE, and changes nothing about the Zariski cover of the base. -/
   103	def IsLocallyCertifiedAff (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
   104	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
   105	    ∀ i : Fin m,
   106	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   107	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   108	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (g i)) n,
   109	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   110	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   111	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   112	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))
   113	
   114	/-- **The widened pin respects divisor equality** — the local `DivEq`s transport through
   115	`divEq_pullback`, verbatim as in the chart-typed case. -/
   116	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   117	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
   118	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d' := by
   119	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
   120	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
   121	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   122	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   123	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
   124	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
   125	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   126	      h _ _)⟩
   127	
   128	/-! ## The comparison with the chart-typed predicate
   129	
   130	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER
   131	sorry-free, and the adaptation's equations and `eqn_rel` transport with it because the pieces
   132	are literally the same opens, only reindexed along `finSumFinEquiv`.
   133	
   134	The migration of the CERTIFICATE is landed too, in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`
   135	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff`, all seven clauses).  Clauses (c1) are `rfl` at the
   136	relabelled index; the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`
   137	in its `symm` direction, which evaluates cast-free, so the intertwining with
   138	`deltaLeft`/`deltaRight` is componentwise and `Module.rankAtStalk` invariance is
   139	`rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv`.  No clause changes, only the index does.
   140	
   141	A predecessor docstring here estimated that transport at about a hundred lines of equalizer
   142	bookkeeping.  That was wrong by an order of magnitude and the reason generalises: arrange the
   143	reindexed cover so its pieces are DEFINITIONALLY the original pieces at the relabelled index,
   144	and the overlap data at `(i, j)` becomes `rfl`-equal to the original at `(e i, e j)`, because
   145	reindexing acts diagonally on the pair index.  Then no intertwining lemma exists to prove. -/
   146	
   147	/-! ## The widened functor value -/
   148	
   149	variable (C R) (n : ℕ)
   150	
   151	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on widened locally-certified systems. -/
   152	def divFamZarAffSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
   153	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} where
   154	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
   155	  iseqv :=
   156	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
   157	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
   158	
   159	/-- **The widened divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (R2, I-0492): locally
   160	certified systems of degree `n` up to divisor equality, where "certified" is now witnessed by
   161	arbitrary affine-open covers of the relative curve.
   162	
   163	This is the carrier that is field-uniform: no hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` appears anywhere in its
   164	definition or in the per-piece layer that produces it. -/
   165	def DivFamZarAff : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
   166	
   167	namespace DivFamZarAff
   168	
   169	variable {C R n}
   170	
   171	/-- The class of a widened locally certified system. -/
   172	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
   173	    DivFamZarAff C R n :=
   174	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarAffSetoid C R n) ⟨d, hd⟩
   175	
   176	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   177	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d₂} :
   178	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
   179	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarAffSetoid C R n)
   180	
   181	/-- **The Picard class of a widened divisor class** `𝒪(D)`, well defined by
   182	`picClass_eq_of_divEq`.  This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes, unchanged by the widening. -/
   183	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
   184	  Quotient.lift
   185	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} =>
   186	      d.1.picClass)
   187	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
   188	
   189	@[simp]
   190	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
   191	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
   192	  rfl
   193	
   194	end DivFamZarAff
   195	
   196	/-! ## The pointwise gate over the widened predicate -/
   197	
   198	variable {C R n}
   199	
   200	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate, widened.** If over every prime of the base there is an
   201	away localization carrying a widened certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the
   202	system is widened-locally certified.  Same quasi-compactness step as
   203	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`): the good
   204	elements' basic opens cover `Spec R`, so finitely many span the unit ideal.
   205	
   206	This is the shape the geometry produces — the support tube isolates pieces over a
   207	neighbourhood of ONE base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime. -/
   208	theorem isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away
   209	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   210	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   211	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   212	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   213	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
   214	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   215	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
   216	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   217	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
   218	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d := by
   219	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
   220	    (fun r =>
   221	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
   222	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
   223	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away r) n,
   224	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   225	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
   226	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   227	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
   228	  exact ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩
   229	
   230	end AlgebraicGeometry

    65	/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended
    66	construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
    67	gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
    68	structure DivRepGlobalData where
    69	  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
    71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
    72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
    73	  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    74	    classify (pull v) = v
    75	  pull_classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T),
    76	    pull (classify F) = F
    77	  pull_comp : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    78	    (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
    79	    pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (pull v)
    80	
    81	namespace DivRepGlobalData
    82	
    83	/-- The general-test equivalence underlying the represented functor. -/
    84	noncomputable def equiv
    85	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    86	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    87	    (T ⟶ DivOver) ≃ divFamZar C pi g T where
    88	  toFun := D.pull
    89	  invFun := D.classify
    90	  left_inv := D.classify_pull
    91	  right_inv := D.pull_classify
    92	
    93	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
    94	@[simp]
    95	theorem equiv_apply
    96	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
    97	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
    98	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T v
    99	      = D.pull v :=
   100	  rfl
   101	
   102	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   103	@[simp]
   104	theorem equiv_symm_apply
   105	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   106	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
   107	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T).symm F
   108	      = D.classify F :=
   109	  rfl
   110	
   111	/-- The final F7 categorical packaging: natural general-test pullback equivalences
   112	represent the locally certified divisor functor by `DivScheme`. -/
   113	noncomputable def representableBy
   114	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2) :
   115	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver where
   116	  homEquiv {T} :=
   117	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T
   118	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
   119	    change D.pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (D.pull v)
   120	    exact D.pull_comp f v
   121	
   122	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   123	@[simp]
   124	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_apply
   125	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   126	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
   127	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
   128	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv v = D.pull v :=
   129	  rfl
   130	
   131	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   132	@[simp]
   133	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_symm_apply
   134	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
   135	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
   136	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
   137	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=
   138	  rfl
   139	
   140	end DivRepGlobalData

   403	/-- Invertibility is stable under transport along a ring equivalence.  The target module
   404	action is the pulled-back action, so this is a direct base-change fact rather than a new
   405	geometric hypothesis. -/
   406	theorem _root_.Module.Invertible.of_ringEquiv
   407	    {S T M : Type u} [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [AddCommGroup M]
   408	    [Module S M] (e : S ≃+* T) [Module.Invertible S M] :
   409	    letI : Algebra S T := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   410	    letI : Module T M := Module.compHom M e.symm.toRingHom
   411	    Module.Invertible T M := by
   412	  letI : Algebra S T := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   413	  letI : Module T M := Module.compHom M e.symm.toRingHom
   414	  letI : IsScalarTower S T M :=
   415	    ⟨fun s t m => by
   416	      change e.symm (e s * t) • m = s • (e.symm t • m)
   417	      rw [map_mul, e.symm_apply_apply, mul_smul]⟩
   418	  letI : Algebra.IsEpi S T :=
   419	    Algebra.isEpi_of_surjective_algebraMap S T (by
   420	      intro t
   421	      refine ⟨e.symm t, ?_⟩
   422	      change e (e.symm t) = t
   423	      exact e.apply_symm_apply t)
   424	  haveI : Module.Invertible T (TensorProduct S T M) := inferInstance
   425	  exact Module.Invertible.congr (TensorProduct.lid' S T M)
   426	
   427	/-- Evaluation at the swallowing piece, with the canonical `A_D`-module action. -/
   428	noncomputable def thetaPieceProdEquivSwallowingPieceOver

   458	/-- The intrinsic theta carrier is invertible over the swallowed equalizer algebra. -/

    12	# The global theta cokernel and the widened intrinsic range
    13

     9	# Widened-adaptation extraction (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	**Every** local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a widened adaptation, with no
    12	chart input whatsoever: `AffAdaptation.exists` below is the R2 counterpart of
    13	`exists_divisorAdaptation` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyExtraction.lean`).
    14	
    15	## Why this is the shape the widening was for
    16	
    17	The chart-typed extraction runs the affine-refinement engine **on each of the two pinned
    18	charts** and glues the results with a partition of unity per chart — the partitions are what
    19	`exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` produces, and they are exactly what protection I-0492
    20	ordered deleted.  Here there is nothing to glue: affine opens form a basis of any scheme
    21	(`Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens`), the relative curve is quasi-compact when `C` is (being a base
    22	change of `C.left`), so one pass gives a finite affine-open cover subordinated to `d.cover`.
    23	No `π`, no charts, no partitions, no `Sum` index.
    24	
    25	The comparison unit is `1` at every piece, as in the chart-typed extraction: the equation is
    26	literally the restriction of `d`'s equation at the anchor.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactRelCurveHom`, `instCompactSpaceRelCurve` — the relative
    31	  curve over a proper `C` is quasi-compact over its test base, hence compact.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affCoverData_subordinate` — a finite affine-open cover with, per
    33	  piece, an anchor point of `d.cover` whose member contains the piece.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation` — hence a widened adaptation of `d`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper` — the same with the compactness
    36	  hypothesis discharged, so with NO hypothesis on the system.
    37	
    38	## What this does and does not close
    39	
    40	It closes the *adaptation* half of the widened lane's producer gap: before this file, the only
    41	way to obtain an `AffAdaptation` was `FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` plus
    42	`DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — i.e. through the chart-typed predicate, which is exactly the route
    43	R2 exists to avoid.  Now a widened adaptation exists for every system, directly.
    44	
    45	It does NOT produce a *certificate*.  The two obligations protection I-0492 clause 4 relocated
    46	— fibrewise-finite support and `SwallowedBy` — remain obligations, and a cover produced by this
    47	extraction has no reason to have a straddling piece.  Producing one that does is where the
    48	Stacks `0B8B` input enters, and that is still owed.

events.text: The “recertify on a swallowed cover” route would need a new finite-support affine-neighborhood theorem and transfer of certificate data, so it is not the cheapest immediate bridge. The existing arbitrary-cover definitions instead expose the canonical descent object: `IntrinsicThetaGluedOver` is a module over the glued divisor algebra, locally invertible on every affine piece. I’m checking whether the project’s descent library can turn those local invertible modules into the missing global projective/rank facts without adding any binder.

    14	/-!
    15	# Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules
    16	
    17	Let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of commutative rings.  This file shows that the
    18	module-theoretic properties *finite*, *finitely presented*, *flat*, *projective* and
    19	*invertible* all descend along `A → B`: if `B ⊗[A] P` has the property over `B`, then `P`
    20	has it over `A`.  Combined with the effectivity theorem of
    21	`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.ModuleDescent` this yields: a `B`-module `M` with a descent
    22	datum descends to an `A`-module `M₀` (unique up to canonical isomorphism), and if `M` is
    23	invertible then so is `M₀`.
    24	
    25	The descent of invertibility is reduced, via the definition
    26	`Module.Invertible R M ↔ Function.Bijective (contractLeft R M)`, to two ingredients:
    27	
    28	* the *dual base-change comparison* `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is an
    29	  isomorphism for `P` finite projective (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`, proved by a
    30	  retract argument from the finite free case, which is `IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight`);
    31	* bijectivity of `A`-linear maps descends along faithfully flat maps
    32	  (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_bijective_iff_bijective`).
    33	
    34	Finiteness and projectivity of `P` are themselves obtained by descent: mathlib provides
    35	finiteness (`Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`) and flatness
    36	(`Module.Flat.of_flat_tensorProduct`); we add finite presentation
    37	(`Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`), and
    38	projectivity follows from flat + finitely presented.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `Module.FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`:
    43	  finite presentation descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    44	* `Module.Projective.of_projective_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: finite projectivity
    45	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    46	* `Module.dualBaseChange A B P : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)`: the dual
    47	  base-change comparison map.
    48	* `Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`: the comparison map is bijective for finite projective
    49	  `P` (over an arbitrary `A`-algebra `B`).
    50	* `Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat`: invertibility
    51	  descends along faithfully flat ring maps.
    52	* `Module.DescentDatum.finite_descended`, `…flat_descended`,
    53	  `…finitePresentation_descended`, `…projective_descended`,
    54	  `…invertible_descended`: for a descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to a
    55	  faithfully flat `A → B`, the descended module inherits each property from `M`;
    56	  in particular **an invertible module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
    57	  module**.
    58	
    59	All modules live in a single universe `u`.
    60	-/

    72	/-- Finite presentation of modules descends along faithfully flat ring maps. -/
    73	theorem FinitePresentation.of_finitePresentation_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
    74	    (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
    75	    [Module.FinitePresentation B (B ⊗[A] P)] :
    76	    Module.FinitePresentation A P := by
    77	  have hfin : Module.Finite A P :=
    78	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
    79	  obtain ⟨n, p, hp⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
    80	  have hpB : Function.Surjective (p.baseChange B) := by
    81	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    82	    exact LinearMap.lTensor_surjective B hp
    83	  have hker : (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)).FG :=
    84	    Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker (p.baseChange B) hpB
    85	  have hexact := Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B p.exact_subtype_ker_map
    86	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B) := by
    87	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    88	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    89	      (LinearMap.ker p).injective_subtype
    90	  have hrange : LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker p).subtype.baseChange B)
    91	      = LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) := by
    92	    ext x
    93	    rw [LinearMap.mem_range, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    94	    constructor
    95	    · rintro ⟨y, rfl⟩
    96	      simp only [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
    97	      exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
    98	    · intro hx
    99	      rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor] at hx
   100	      obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact x).mp hx
   101	      exact ⟨y, by rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]; exact hy⟩
   102	  have e : (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) ≃ₗ[B] LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B) :=
   103	    (LinearEquiv.ofInjective _ hinj).trans (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ hrange)
   104	  have : Module.Finite B (LinearMap.ker (p.baseChange B)) := Module.Finite.iff_fg.mpr hker
   105	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] LinearMap.ker p) := Module.Finite.equiv e.symm
   106	  have : Module.Finite A (LinearMap.ker p) :=
   107	    Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B
   108	  exact Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective p hp (Module.Finite.iff_fg.mp this)

   124	section DualBaseChange

   126	variable {A B} in
   127	/-- Two `B`-functionals on `B ⊗[A] X` that agree on the tensors `1 ⊗ₜ x` are equal. -/
   128	private theorem dual_ext {X : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
   129	    {F G : Dual B (B ⊗[A] X)} (h : ∀ x : X, F (1 ⊗ₜ x) = G (1 ⊗ₜ x)) : F = G := by
   130	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   131	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   132	  intro b x
   133	  have hb : b ⊗ₜ[A] x = b • (1 ⊗ₜ[A] x : B ⊗[A] X) := by
   134	    rw [TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, mul_one]
   135	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, hb, map_smul, h]
   136	
   137	variable (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   138	
   139	/-- The canonical `B`-linear comparison map from the base change of the dual to the dual
   140	of the base change, `b ⊗ₜ f ↦ b • (f.baseChange B)`.  It is bijective for finite
   141	projective `P` (`Module.bijective_dualBaseChange`). -/
   142	noncomputable def dualBaseChange : B ⊗[A] Dual A P →ₗ[B] Dual B (B ⊗[A] P) :=
   143	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (Module.Dual.baseChange B)
   144	
   145	@[simp] theorem dualBaseChange_tmul (b : B) (f : Dual A P) :
   146	    dualBaseChange A B P (b ⊗ₜ f) = b • Module.Dual.baseChange B f := rfl
   147	
   148	/-- Naturality of the dual base-change comparison map. -/
   149	theorem dualBaseChange_naturality {P Q : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P]
   150	    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q] (g : P →ₗ[A] Q) :
   151	    dualBaseChange A B P ∘ₗ g.dualMap.baseChange B =
   152	      (g.baseChange B).dualMap ∘ₗ dualBaseChange A B Q := by
   153	  apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   154	  apply TensorProduct.ext'
   155	  intro b f
   156	  simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   157	  refine dual_ext fun x => ?_
   158	  simp [Module.Dual.baseChange_apply_tmul]
   159	
   160	variable {A B} in
   161	private theorem bijective_dualBaseChange_free (n : ℕ) :
   162	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A)) := by
   163	  have j : IsBaseChange B (TensorProduct.mk A B (Fin n → A) 1) :=
   164	    TensorProduct.isBaseChange A (Fin n → A) B
   165	  have k : IsBaseChange B (Algebra.linearMap A B) := IsBaseChange.linearMap A B
   166	  have hlr : IsBaseChange B (IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B)) :=
   167	    IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRight j k
   168	  have heq : Module.Dual.baseChange (R := A) B (V := Fin n → A)
   169	      = IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom j (Algebra.linearMap A B) := by
   170	    refine LinearMap.ext fun f => dual_ext fun x => ?_
   171	    have h1 := IsBaseChange.linearMapLeftRightHom_comp_apply j (Algebra.linearMap A B) f x
   172	    simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using h1.symm
   173	  have hlift : dualBaseChange A B (Fin n → A) = hlr.equiv.toLinearMap := by
   174	    apply LinearMap.restrictScalars_injective A
   175	    apply TensorProduct.ext'
   176	    intro b f
   177	    simp only [LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, dualBaseChange_tmul,
   178	      IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul, heq]
   179	  rw [hlift]
   180	  exact hlr.equiv.bijective
   181	
   182	/-- **The dual commutes with base change for finite projective modules**: the comparison
   183	map `B ⊗[A] Dual A P → Dual B (B ⊗[A] P)` is bijective when `P` is finite projective. -/
   184	theorem bijective_dualBaseChange [Module.Finite A P] [Projective A P] :
   185	    Function.Bijective (dualBaseChange A B P) := by
   186	  obtain ⟨n, r, hr⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin' A P
   187	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property r LinearMap.id hr
   188	  have hfree := bijective_dualBaseChange_free (A := A) (B := B) n
   189	  have hnat_r := dualBaseChange_naturality A B r
   190	  have hnat_s := dualBaseChange_naturality A B s
   191	  -- the two retraction identities
   192	  have hcomp : s.dualMap ∘ₗ r.dualMap = LinearMap.id := by
   193	    ext f x
   194	    simpa using congrArg f (LinearMap.congr_fun hs x)
   195	  have hu : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] Dual A P,
   196	      s.dualMap.baseChange B (r.dualMap.baseChange B x) = x := by
   197	    intro x

   227	faithfully flat and `B ⊗[A] P` is an invertible `B`-module, then `P` is an invertible
   228	`A`-module. -/

   253	    rw [hsquare]

   256	        (Module.Invertible.bijective (R := B) (M := B ⊗[A] P))).comp
   257	        ((Module.Invertible.rTensor_bijective_iff (M := B ⊗[A] P)).mpr
   258	          (bijective_dualBaseChange A B P))).comp
   259	      (AlgebraTensorModule.distribBaseChange A B (Dual A P) P).bijective

   275	  have : Module.Flat B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv D.descentEquiv

   279	    Module.FinitePresentation A D.descended := by

   288	    Projective A D.descended := by
   289	  have : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] D.descended) := Module.Finite.equiv D.descentEquiv.symm

   293	/-- **Faithfully flat descent of invertible modules**: if `M` is an invertible `B`-module

   179	theorem divFamEps_carvePairArrow_mapAlg (F : DivFam C S π g)
   180	    (μ : ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
   181	        (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤) →ₗ[k]
   182	      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
   183	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤))
   184	    (h : carvePairArrow μ (divFamEps hπ g F).1 (divFamEps hπ g F).2 = 0)
   185	    (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra k T] [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower k S T] :
   186	    carvePairArrow μ (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).1
   187	      (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).2 = 0 := by
   188	  haveI hp₁ : Module.Projective S
   189	      ((TensorProduct k S ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
   190	        (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸ (divFamEps hπ g F).1) :=
   191	    DivFam.projective_window_quotient hπ g hO hχ (windowM_choice π hπ g)
   192	      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) le_rfl F
   193	  haveI hp₂ : Module.Projective S
   194	      ((TensorProduct k S ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
   195	        ((windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g) • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸
   196	        (divFamEps hπ g F).2) :=
   197	    DivFam.projective_window_quotient hπ g hO hχ
   198	      (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)
   199	      (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g) (Nat.le_add_right _ _) F
   200	  have h0 : LinearMap.baseChange T
   201	      (carvePairArrow μ (divFamEps hπ g F).1 (divFamEps hπ g F).2) = 0 := by
   202	    rw [h, LinearMap.baseChange_zero]
   203	  have h1 := (baseChange_carvePairArrow_eq_zero_iff T μ
   204	    (divFamEps hπ g F).1 (divFamEps hπ g F).2).mp h0
   205	  have h2 : (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).1
   206	      = LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ T (divFamEps hπ g F).1) :=
   207	    (DivFam.window_mapAlg hπ g hO hχ (windowM_choice π hπ g)
   208	      (relThetaPairH1_windowM C π hπ g) le_rfl T F).trans
   209	      (windowBaseChange_eq_ker_baseChangeMkQ T (divFamEps hπ g F).1)
   210	  have h3 : (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).2
   211	      = LinearMap.ker (Module.Grassmannian.baseChangeMkQ T (divFamEps hπ g F).2) :=
   212	    (DivFam.window_mapAlg hπ g hO hχ
   213	      (windowM_choice π hπ g + windowS_choice π hπ g)
   214	      (relThetaPairH1_windowMS C π hπ g) (Nat.le_add_right _ _) T F).trans
   215	      (windowBaseChange_eq_ker_baseChangeMkQ T (divFamEps hπ g F).2)
   216	  rw [h2, h3]
   217	  exact h1

   236	/-- **The per-piece classify `vₜ`** (`informal/w4-g5-worksheet.md` §2): a divisor
   237	family `F` over `S` whose ε pair satisfies the carve, together with a pair-chart
   238	framing of the restricted ε pair over an `S`-tower test `T` (the
   239	`divFamEps_exists_frameCover` output shape at `T = Localization.Away (f t)`),
   240	factors uniquely through `divSchemeι` over the pair chart — `divClassifyAff` at
   241	`DivFam.mapAlg T g F` with the transported carve.  No Noetherian hypotheses
   242	(w4-ddr9 §0.4). -/
   243	theorem divClassifyLocal (F : DivFam C S π g)
   244	    (hcarve : ∀ a : ↥(divisorSections k
   245	        (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤),
   246	      carvePairArrow (windowShiftMul hπ g a)
   247	        (divFamEps hπ g F).1 (divFamEps hπ g F).2 = 0)
   248	    (T : Type u) [CommRing T] [Algebra k T] [Algebra S T] [IsScalarTower k S T]
   249	    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
   250	    (w : PairChartRing k g r₁ g r₂ i j →ₐ[k] T)
   251	    (hw₁ : (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautFst k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
   252	      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T b₁.equivFun.toLinearMap)
   253	          (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).1)
   254	    (hw₂ : (Module.Grassmannian.map w (pairTautSnd k g r₁ r₂ i j)).toSubmodule
   255	      = Submodule.map (LinearMap.baseChange T b₂.equivFun.toLinearMap)
   256	          (divFamEps hπ g (DivFam.mapAlg T g F)).2) :
   257	    ∃! v : Spec (CommRingCat.of T) ⟶
   258	        DivScheme k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   259	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
   260	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm),
   261	      v ≫ divSchemeι k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   262	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
   263	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)
   264	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom w.toRingHom) ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
   265	  divClassifyAff hπ g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ (DivFam.mapAlg T g F) i j w hw₁ hw₂
   266	    (fun a => divFamEps_carvePairArrow_mapAlg hπ g hO hχ F (windowShiftMul hπ g a)
   267	      (hcarve a) T)
   268	
   269	end Classify

    11	# F4 — the backward direction of `divRepAff` at the Zar layer
    12	(`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §2.1, steps 1, 3, 5, 6)
    13	
    14	A locally certified divisor class `F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g` over an affine test `S`
    15	classifies to a **unique** morphism `overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver g` — the content of
    16	`divRepAff.symm`.  Construction: the composite certificate × frame cover of the Kit
    17	(`DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover`), `divClassify` fired at each certified
    18	representative with the carve discharged by DDR-9.0 (`divFamEps_carve`), the glue by
    19	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` with overlap agreement through the clause-transport
    20	layer, and the Over packaging by `divSchemeOverHomMk` (F2).
    21	
    22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsDivRepClassify` — **the characterizing clause** (the
    23	  refinement-stable form F6 consumes): over EVERY `k`/`S`-tower test `T` carrying a
    24	  certified representative `G` of the restricted class and a pair-chart framing of
    25	  `ε (DivFam.mk G)`, the morphism chart-factors.  No localization hypothesis on `T`
    26	  — stability under refinement of covers and change of representative is built into
    27	  the quantifier.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divClassifyZar` — **the ∃!-keystone**: `F₀` classifies to a
    29	  unique clause-satisfier `Spec S ⟶ DivScheme g` (overlap layer:
    30	  `Picard/DivRepClassifyZarCompat.lean`).
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepClassifyZar` — **the keystone map**
    32	  `DivFamZar C S π g → (overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver g)`, with the characterizing
    33	  lemma `divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify` and the well-definedness lemma
    34	  `divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify` (any Over-hom whose scheme morphism
    35	  satisfies the clause IS the classified one — Law 2's uniqueness input).

   138	  choose v hvc using hv

   141	          (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.f p)

   143	          (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.f q) ≫ v p

   145	    pullback_divClassifyClause_compat hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀
   146	      (DivFam.mk (G p)) (DivFam.mk (G q)) (hZ p) (hZ q) (hvc p) (hvc q)
   147	  refine ⟨(Scheme.affineOpenCoverOfSpanRangeEqTop
   148	    (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover.glueMorphisms v hglue, ?_⟩
   149	  intro T _ _ _ _ GT hGT i j ω hω₁ hω₂

   180	      (R := CommRingCat.of S) r hspan).openCover _ _ fun p => ?_

   195	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm)

   202	include hO hχ in
   203	/-- **The ∃!-keystone of the backward direction** (w4-ddr9 §2.1): a locally

   206	theorem divClassifyZar (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g) :
   207	    ∃! v : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
   208	        DivScheme k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)

   219	/-- **The classified morphism, packaged over `Spec k`**: the clause-satisfier carries

   221	certificate × frame cover, so `divSchemeOverHomMk` (F2) applies. -/
   222	theorem exists_overHom_isDivRepClassify (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π g) :
   223	    ∃ u : overSpec k S ⟶
   224	        divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   225	          (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
   226	          (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm),

   228	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_isDivRepClassify hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀
   229	  obtain ⟨m, r, hspan, hdata⟩ :=
   230	    DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover hπ g hO hχ r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ F₀
   231	  choose G ci cj cw hZ hcw₁ hcw₂ using hdata
   232	  exact ⟨divSchemeOverHomMk k (windowS_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   233	    (windowM_choice π hπ g • fiberWeilDivisor π) g r₁ r₂ b₁
   234	    (b₂.map (windowShiftEquiv hπ g).symm) v r hspan
   235	    (fun p => ⟨ci p, cj p, cw p,
   236	      hv (Localization.Away (r p)) (G p) (hZ p) (ci p) (cj p) (cw p)
   237	        (hcw₁ p) (hcw₂ p)⟩), hv⟩

     9	/-!
    10	# The per-piece descent datum ((C2) effectivity, brick E2 — the algebraic core)
    11	
    12	The (C2) effectivity campaign descends a rigidified class `L` on the curve `X_B` over the
    13	étale cover `Spec B` along the cover inclusion `cg`, piece by piece over a `cg`-saturated
    14	affine cover `{V}` of the base curve `X_A` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityPieces`,
    15	brick E0).  On a piece `V` the cover ring is `M := Γ(V) ⊗[A] B` (`Over.pieceEquiv`), and
    16	the descent along `Γ(V) → M` is governed by the σ-normalized comparison cochain `θ` of
    17	`AlgebraicGeometry.NormalizedCechComparison` (brick E1) restricted to the piece.  This
    18	file supplies the **pure-algebra bridge** the per-piece descent runs on: the
    19	identification of the descent-cocycle ring with the geometric double-base ring, and the
    20	extraction of a `Module.IsDescentCocycle` from a comparison unit in geometric
    21	coordinates.
    22	
    23	For a commutative ring `A`, an `A`-algebra `S` (the base-piece ring `Γ(V)`) and an
    24	`A`-algebra `B` (the étale cover), writing `M := S ⊗[A] B` for the cover-piece ring:
    25	
    26	* `Algebra.TensorProduct.pieceDescentEquiv A S B : (M ⊗[S] M) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` —
    27	  **the descent-cocycle ring identification** (D2's frontier item 1): the ring
    28	  `M ⊗[S] M` in which a `Module.IsDescentCocycle` lives is, on the nose, the base change
    29	  to `S` of the descent-cocycle ring `B ⊗[A] B` of the whole cover.  On pure tensors
    30	  `(s₁ ⊗ b₁) ⊗ (s₂ ⊗ b₂) ↦ (s₂ * s₁) ⊗ (b₁ ⊗ b₂)` (`pieceDescentEquiv_tmul`);
    31	* `Algebra.TensorProduct.pieceDescentTripleEquiv` — the triple analogue
    32	  `M ⊗[S] (M ⊗[S] M) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))`, carrying the Amitsur cocycle
    33	  identity;
    34	* `pieceDescentEquiv_lmul'` / `pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₂₃/₁₂/₁₃` — **the
    35	  coprojection–face compatibility**: the identification intertwines the multiplication
    36	  `lmul'` and the three simplicial cofaces `descentFace` of `M ⊗[S] M` with the
    37	  base-changed maps `id_S ⊗ lmul'` and `id_S ⊗ descentFace` of `S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.
    38	
    39	The payload is the extraction:
    40	
    41	* `Module.comparisonDescentUnit A S B v : (M ⊗[S] M)ˣ` for a **comparison unit**
    42	  `v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ` — the value `pieceEquiv` transports the piece restriction of
    43	  the E1 comparison to — and
    44	* `Module.isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit`: if `v` is diagonal-normalized
    45	  (`id_S ⊗ lmul'` sends it to `1` — the cochain source is
    46	  `Over.normalizedComparison_diagonal_eq_one`) and satisfies the Amitsur cocycle identity
    47	  through the three cofaces (the cochain source is `NormalizedCechComparison.coherent`),
    48	  then `comparisonDescentUnit A S B v` is a `Module.IsDescentCocycle` over `S → M`;
    49	* `Module.comparisonDescentClass` — its Picard class `∈ CommRing.Pic S`, the descended
    50	  per-piece class `M_V` (for faithfully flat `A → B`).
    51	
    52	## The frontier consumed by E3
    53	
    54	Producing the comparison unit `v` from the piece restriction of `θ` is a gluing step
    55	(the restricted `θ`, twisted by a trivialization of `L` on the affine piece, glues to a
    56	single unit of `Γ(cg⁻¹ V ×_{Spec A} Spec (B ⊗[A] B))` by the `𝒪ˣ`-sheaf axiom, exactly as
    57	the (C1) `witnessBasicSection` construction of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.WitnessCorrection`
    58	does for the trivial-on-cover case); the diagonal and Amitsur hypotheses on `v` are then
    59	the restrictions of `Over.normalizedComparison_diagonal_eq_one` and
    60	`NormalizedCechComparison.coherent`.  The restriction compatibility on overlaps `W ≤ V`
    61	(D2 item 3b) is `Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_baseChange`
    62	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescentBaseChange`) along `Over.resAlgHomA : Γ(V) →ₐ[A]
    63	Γ(W)`, once the two comparison units are related by base change through
    64	`Over.pieceRingEquiv_naturality`.
    65	-/

    78	
    79	/-- **The descent-cocycle ring identification** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): for an
    80	`A`-algebra `S` (the base-piece ring) and an `A`-algebra `B` (the cover), the ring
    81	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)` in which a `Module.IsDescentCocycle` over `S → S ⊗[A] B`
    82	lives is the base change to `S` of the whole-cover descent-cocycle ring `B ⊗[A] B`:
    83	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)`.  The composite of mathlib's
    84	`cancelBaseChange` (cancelling the middle `S`) and `assoc`. -/
    85	noncomputable def pieceDescentEquiv :
    86	    (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B) :=
    87	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange A S S (S ⊗[A] B) B).trans
    88	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc A A S S B B)

    90	@[simp]
    91	lemma pieceDescentEquiv_tmul (s₁ s₂ : S) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    92	    pieceDescentEquiv A S B ((s₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₁) ⊗ₜ[S] (s₂ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂))
    93	      = (s₂ * s₁) ⊗ₜ[A] (b₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂) := by
    94	  simp only [pieceDescentEquiv, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, cancelBaseChange_tmul,
    95	    TensorProduct.smul_tmul', smul_eq_mul, Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc_tmul]
    96	
    97	/-- The first coprojection step of `pieceDescentTripleEquiv`, on a pure `S`-tensor:
    98	`congr (refl) pieceDescentEquiv (a ⊗ x) = a ⊗ pieceDescentEquiv x`. -/
    99	private lemma congr_refl_pieceDescentEquiv (a : S ⊗[A] B)
   100	    (x : (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)) :
   101	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr (AlgEquiv.refl (R := S) (A₁ := S ⊗[A] B))
   102	        (pieceDescentEquiv A S B)) (a ⊗ₜ[S] x)
   103	      = a ⊗ₜ[S] pieceDescentEquiv A S B x := by
   104	  rw [congr_apply, Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul]; rfl
   105	
   106	/-- **The triple descent-cocycle ring identification**: the base of the Amitsur cocycle
   107	identity, `(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)) ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))`. -/
   108	noncomputable def pieceDescentTripleEquiv :
   109	    (S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B))
   110	      ≃ₐ[S] S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)) :=
   111	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.congr (AlgEquiv.refl (R := S) (A₁ := S ⊗[A] B))
   112	      (pieceDescentEquiv A S B)).trans
   113	    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange A S S (S ⊗[A] B) (B ⊗[A] B)).trans
   114	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.assoc A A S S B (B ⊗[A] B)))

   117	lemma pieceDescentTripleEquiv_tmul (s₀ s₁ s₂ : S) (b₀ b₁ b₂ : B) :
   118	    pieceDescentTripleEquiv A S B
   119	        ((s₀ ⊗ₜ[A] b₀) ⊗ₜ[S] ((s₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₁) ⊗ₜ[S] (s₂ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂)))
   120	      = (s₂ * s₁ * s₀) ⊗ₜ[A] (b₀ ⊗ₜ[A] (b₁ ⊗ₜ[A] b₂)) := by
   121	  rw [pieceDescentTripleEquiv, AlgEquiv.trans_apply, AlgEquiv.trans_apply,

   144	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.add_tmul, map_add, hx, hy]
   145	    | zero => simp only [TensorProduct.zero_tmul, map_zero]
   146	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
   147	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]

   216	/-! ## The cover-pullback triviality of a descended class
   217	
   218	The image of the Picard class of a descent cocycle under base change to the cover is
   219	trivial: the descended module base-changes back to the cover ring itself. -/
   220	
   221	/-- **The cover-pullback of a descended class is trivial**: for a faithfully flat cover
   222	`R → T`, base change of the Picard class of a descent cocycle back up to `T` is `1`, since
   223	the descended module base-changes to `T` through `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv`.  On a
   224	`cg`-saturated affine piece `V` (with `R = Γ(V)`, `T = Γ(V) ⊗[A] B ≅ Γ(cg⁻¹ V)`) this is
   225	the provable half of the D2 item-3a cg-pullback recovery: the descended class `M_V` pulls
   226	back to the trivial class on the cover piece. -/
   227	theorem IsDescentCocycle.mapAlgebra_picClass_eq_one {R T : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing T]
   228	    [Algebra R T] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R T] {u : (T ⊗[R] T)ˣ}
   229	    (hu : Module.IsDescentCocycle u) :
   230	    CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra R T hu.picClass = 1 := by
   231	  rw [Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass, CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra_apply,
   232	    CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_one_iff]
   233	  exact ⟨(LinearEquiv.baseChange R T (CommRing.Pic.mk R hu.descended).AsModule hu.descended
   234	      (CommRing.Pic.mk.linearEquiv R hu.descended)).trans
   235	    (Module.DescentDatum.ofUnit u hu).descentEquiv⟩

   239	/-! ## The per-piece descent unit and its cocycle property -/
   240	
   241	/-- **The per-piece descent unit** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): the unit of
   242	`(S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B)` corresponding to a comparison unit
   243	`v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ` under the descent-cocycle ring identification
   244	`pieceDescentEquiv`.  On a piece `V`, `v` is the value `Over.pieceEquiv` transports the
   245	piece restriction of the E1 comparison `θ` to. -/
   246	noncomputable def comparisonDescentUnit (v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ) :
   247	    ((S ⊗[A] B) ⊗[S] (S ⊗[A] B))ˣ :=
   248	  Units.map (pieceDescentEquiv A S B).symm.toAlgHom.toRingHom.toMonoidHom v
   249	
   250	@[simp]
   251	lemma pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val (v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ) :
   252	    pieceDescentEquiv A S B (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v).val = v.val := by
   253	  change pieceDescentEquiv A S B ((pieceDescentEquiv A S B).symm v.val) = v.val
   254	  exact AlgEquiv.apply_symm_apply _ _
   255	
   256	/-- **The per-piece descent unit of a coherent comparison unit is a descent 1-cocycle**
   257	((C2) effectivity, brick E2).  The diagonal normalization is the `id_S ⊗ lmul'`
   258	hypothesis `hlmul` — the cochain source is `Over.normalizedComparison_diagonal_eq_one`
   259	restricted to the piece; the cocycle identity is the Amitsur identity through the three
   260	cofaces `hcoc` — the cochain source is `NormalizedCechComparison.coherent`.  Both are
   261	transported through the descent-cocycle ring identifications by the coprojection–face
   262	compatibility lemmas. -/
   263	theorem isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   264	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   265	      = 1)
   266	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   267	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   268	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   269	    Module.IsDescentCocycle (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v) where
   270	  lmul'_eq_one := by
   271	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' S (S := S ⊗[A] B)
   272	      (comparisonDescentUnit A S B v).val = 1
   273	    rw [pieceDescentEquiv_lmul', pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val, hlmul]
   274	  cocycle := by
   275	    apply (pieceDescentTripleEquiv A S B).injective
   276	    rw [map_mul, pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₂₃,
   277	      pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₁₂, pieceDescentTripleEquiv_descentFace₁₃,
   278	      pieceDescentEquiv_comparisonDescentUnit_val, hcoc]

   280	/-! ## The descended per-piece Picard class -/

   282	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
   283	
   284	/-- **The descended per-piece class `M_V`** ((C2) effectivity, brick E2): for a faithfully
   285	flat cover `A → B` and a coherent comparison unit `v`, the Picard class over the base
   286	piece `S = Γ(V)` of the module descended from the per-piece descent cocycle.  Its image
   287	under `CommRing.Pic S → CommRing.Pic (S ⊗[A] B)` is trivial (the descent recovers the
   288	cover-piece ring `M = S ⊗[A] B` twisted by the comparison), so the tracked cg-pullback
   289	recovery of D2 item 3a is the identification of `L` restricted to the piece with the
   290	comparison twist; the restriction compatibility on overlaps (D2 item 3b) is
   291	`Module.IsDescentCocycle.picClass_baseChange`. -/
   292	noncomputable def comparisonDescentClass {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   293	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   294	      = 1)
   295	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   296	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   297	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   298	    CommRing.Pic S :=
   299	  (isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit A S B hlmul hcoc).picClass
   300	
   301	/-- **The cg-pullback recovery of the descended per-piece class** (D2 item 3a, provable
   302	half): the descended class `comparisonDescentClass` pulls back to the trivial class on the
   303	cover-piece ring `S ⊗[A] B ≅ Γ(cg⁻¹ V)`.  The full D2 item-3a — that this trivial
   304	cover-pullback *is* the class of `L` restricted to the piece — is the statement that the
   305	comparison unit `v` trivializes `L` on the piece, established when `v` is produced from the
   306	piece restriction of the E1 comparison (the frontier consumed by E3). -/
   307	theorem mapAlgebra_comparisonDescentClass_eq_one {v : (S ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B))ˣ}
   308	    (hlmul : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A) v.val
   309	      = 1)
   310	    (hcoc : Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₂₃ A B) v.val
   311	          * Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₂ A B) v.val
   312	        = Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id S S) (Module.descentFace₁₃ A B) v.val) :
   313	    CommRing.Pic.mapAlgebra S (S ⊗[A] B) (comparisonDescentClass A S B hlmul hcoc) = 1 :=
   314	  (isDescentCocycle_comparisonDescentUnit A S B hlmul hcoc).mapAlgebra_picClass_eq_one
   315	
   316	end Module

     8	/-!
     9	# The intrinsic theta Cech equalizer over the widened colength algebra
    10	
    11	The intrinsic piece and overlap quotients of `DivisorFamilyAffThetaDescent` are modules over
    12	different local colength algebras. This file restricts all of those actions to the single
    13	widened equalizer algebra `A_D = gluedSubalgebra A`. The two overlap restrictions then become
    14	`A_D`-linear maps, and the intrinsic theta module is their kernel in `A_D`-modules.
    15	
    16	The final declarations give the resulting equalizer its universal property. This is the
    17	module-descent input needed to compare the intrinsic theta line with its piecewise base
    18	changes and descend invertibility, without a `ChartTyping` or any additional hypothesis.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	
    23	universe u
    24	
    25	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    26	
    27	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    28	
    29	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    32	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    33	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	variable {D : AffCoverData C R} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
    35	
    36	namespace AffAdaptation

    38	attribute [local instance] thetaPieceQuotientModule thetaOverlapQuotientModule
    39	
    40	/-- Restriction of the widened equalizer algebra to one overlap colength algebra. -/
    41	noncomputable def gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    42	    ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
    43	  (A.toOvlLeft i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap i)
    44	
    45	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
    46	/-- The overlap algebra map is independent of whether it is evaluated through the left or
    47	right piece. This is exactly the defining equalizer relation of `A_D`. -/
    48	lemma gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap_eq_right (A : AffAdaptation D d) (i j : D.index) :
    49	    A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j =
    50	      (A.toOvlRight i j).comp (A.gluedSubalgebraPieceMap j) := by
    51	  ext c
    52	  change A.toOvlLeft i j (c.1 i) = A.toOvlRight i j (c.1 j)
    53	  exact (A.mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (c : A.chartProd)).mp c.2 (i, j)
    54	
    55	/-- An overlap theta quotient, restricted to an `A_D`-module through the common overlap
    56	algebra map. -/
    57	@[reducible]
    58	noncomputable def thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    59	    (i j : D.index) :
    60	    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    61	      (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    62	  letI : Module (A.ovlColength i j) (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j) :=
    63	    A.thetaOverlapQuotientModule (π := π) a i j
    64	  Module.compHom (A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j)
    65	    (A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j).toRingHom
    66	
    67	attribute [local instance] thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule
    68	  thetaOverlapQuotientGluedModule
    69	
    70	/-- The intrinsic theta equalizer carries its canonical module structure over the widened
    71	colength algebra outside this construction file as well. -/
    72	@[reducible]
    73	noncomputable instance intrinsicThetaGluedOverModule (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
    74	    Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a) :=
    75	  letI : ∀ j, Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    76	      (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j) :=
    77	    fun j => A.thetaPieceQuotientGluedModule (π := π) a j
    78	  Submodule.module (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a)
    79	
    80	/-- The left piece-to-overlap restriction as an `A_D`-linear map. -/
    81	noncomputable def thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    82	    (i j : D.index) :
    83	    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a i →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
    84	      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
    85	  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j
    86	  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j).map_add
    87	  map_smul' := by
    88	    intro c x
    89	    change A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j (c.1 i • x) =
    90	      A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j c •
    91	        A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a i j x
    92	    rw [A.thetaToOverlapLeft_smul]
    93	    rfl
    94	
    95	/-- The right piece-to-overlap restriction as an `A_D`-linear map. -/
    96	noncomputable def thetaToOverlapRightGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
    97	    (i j : D.index) :
    98	    A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
    99	      A.ThetaOverlapQuotient (π := π) a i j where
   100	  toFun := A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j
   101	  map_add' := (A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j).map_add
   102	  map_smul' := by
   103	    intro c x
   104	    change A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j (c.1 j • x) =
   105	      A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap i j c •
   106	        A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a i j x
   107	    rw [A.thetaToOverlapRight_smul]
   108	    rw [A.gluedSubalgebraOverlapMap_eq_right i j]
   109	    rfl
   110	
   111	/-- The left arrow of the intrinsic theta descent fork in `A_D`-modules. -/
   112	noncomputable def thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   113	    A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   114	      A.ThetaOverlapProd (π := π) a :=
   115	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   116	    A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a p.1 p.2 ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   117	
   118	/-- The right arrow of the intrinsic theta descent fork in `A_D`-modules. -/
   119	noncomputable def thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   120	    A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   121	      A.ThetaOverlapProd (π := π) a :=
   122	  LinearMap.pi (fun p : D.index × D.index =>
   123	    A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a p.1 p.2 ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   124	
   125	/-- The kernel of the intrinsic theta descent fork, formed in `A_D`-modules. -/
   126	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   127	    Submodule ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) (A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) :=
   128	  LinearMap.ker (A.thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued (π := π) a -
   129	    A.thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued (π := π) a)
   130	
   131	/-- Membership in the `A_D`-linear kernel is pairwise equality on overlaps. -/
   132	lemma mem_intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver_iff (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   133	    (s : A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) :
   134	    s ∈ A.intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (π := π) a ↔
   135	      ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   136	        A.thetaToOverlapLeft (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (s p.1) =
   137	          A.thetaToOverlapRight (π := π) a p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   138	  simp only [intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply,
   139	    sub_eq_zero, funext_iff, thetaIntrinsicDeltaLeftGlued,
   140	    thetaIntrinsicDeltaRightGlued, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   141	    Function.comp_apply, thetaToOverlapLeftGlued,
   142	    thetaToOverlapRightGlued]
   143	  rfl
   144	
   145	/-- The previously constructed intrinsic theta `A_D`-module is exactly the kernel of the
   146	`A_D`-linear descent fork. -/
   147	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedOver_eq_ker (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ) :
   148	    A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a =
   149	      A.intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver (π := π) a := by
   150	  ext s
   151	  change s ∈ A.intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule (π := π) a ↔ _
   152	  rw [A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff,
   153	    A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedKernelOver_iff]
   154	
   155	/-- Projection of the intrinsic theta equalizer to one piece quotient. -/
   156	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   157	    (j : D.index) :
   158	    A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   159	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j :=
   160	  LinearMap.proj j ∘ₗ (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a).subtype
   161	
   162	/-- The piece projections from the intrinsic theta equalizer agree on every overlap. -/
   163	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece_overlap (A : AffAdaptation D d) (a : ℕ)
   164	    (i j : D.index) :
   165	    A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ
   166	        A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a i =
   167	      A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ
   168	        A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a j := by
   169	  apply LinearMap.ext
   170	  intro x
   171	  exact (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a _).mp x.2 (i, j)

   173	section Universal
   174	
   175	variable (A : AffAdaptation D d)
   176	variable {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M]
   177	  [Module ↥(gluedSubalgebra A) M]
   178	
   179	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   180	-- The nested dependent-product module action exceeds the default instance-search budget.
   181	/-- A compatible family of `A_D`-linear maps to the piece theta quotients factors through
   182	the intrinsic theta equalizer. -/
   183	noncomputable def intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (a : ℕ)
   184	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   185	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   186	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   187	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   188	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j) :
   189	    M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   190	      A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a where
   191	  toFun x := ⟨fun j => f j x, by
   192	    apply (A.mem_intrinsicThetaGluedSubmodule_iff (π := π) a _).mpr
   193	    rintro ⟨i, j⟩
   194	    exact LinearMap.congr_fun (hf i j) x⟩
   195	  map_add' x y := by
   196	    apply Subtype.ext
   197	    funext j
   198	    exact (f j).map_add x y
   199	  map_smul' c x := by
   200	    apply Subtype.ext
   201	    funext j
   202	    exact (f j).map_smul c x
   203	
   204	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   205	-- The statement unfolds the same nested dependent-product module action as the lift.
   206	@[simp]
   207	lemma intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift_apply (a : ℕ)
   208	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   209	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   210	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   211	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   212	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j)
   213	    (x : M) (j : D.index) :
   214	    (A.intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (π := π) a f hf x :
   215	      A.ThetaPieceProd (π := π) a) j = f j x := by
   216	  rfl
   217	
   218	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in
   219	-- Comparing the two dependent-product linear maps needs the lift's instance-search budget.
   220	/-- The compatible-family lift is the unique `A_D`-linear map with the prescribed piece
   221	projections. -/
   222	theorem intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift_unique (a : ℕ)
   223	    (f : ∀ j : D.index, M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   224	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := π) a j)
   225	    (hf : ∀ i j : D.index,
   226	      A.thetaToOverlapLeftGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f i =
   227	        A.thetaToOverlapRightGlued (π := π) a i j ∘ₗ f j)
   228	    (g : M →ₗ[↥(gluedSubalgebra A)]
   229	      A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a)
   230	    (hg : ∀ j : D.index,
   231	      A.intrinsicThetaGluedToPiece (π := π) a j ∘ₗ g = f j) :
   232	    g = A.intrinsicThetaGluedOverLift (π := π) a f hf := by
   233	  apply LinearMap.ext
   234	  intro x
   235	  apply Subtype.ext
   236	  funext j
   237	  exact LinearMap.congr_fun (hg j) x
   238

170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
   171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
   172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
   173	
   174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
   175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
   176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
   177	  Ideal.span
   178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
   179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
   180	
   181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
   182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
   183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
   184	
   185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
   186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
   188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
   189	    (by
   190	      intro a ha
   191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
   196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
   198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   199	
   200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
   201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   204	    (by
   205	      intro a ha
   206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   214	
   215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
   216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
   217	
   218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
   219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   220	
   221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
   222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   223	  LinearMap.pi
   224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   225	
   226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
   227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   228	  LinearMap.pi
   229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   230	
   231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
   232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
   233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
   235	
   236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
   237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
   239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   240	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   241	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   242	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   243	
   244	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   245	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
   246	
   247	/-! ### The certificate -/
   248	
   249	/-- **The colength certificate over a widened cover** — clauses (c1)–(c4) verbatim from
   250	`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`.  Nothing is added and nothing is dropped: the widening
   251	changes where the pieces LIVE, not what the certificate asserts. -/
   252	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   253	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   254	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
   255	  /-- (c1) Each piece-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   256	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   257	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   258	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   259	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   260	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
   261	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
   262	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
   263	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
   264	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
   265	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
   266	  flat_coker_diff :
   267	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
   268	
   269	end AffAdaptation
   270	
   271	end AlgebraicGeometry

events.text: A direct precedent exists in the chart-typed carrier: `DivisorFamilyThetaRank.lean` already proves that the theta equalizer is invertible over the glued colength algebra, then derives finite/projective/rank over the base. I’m reading that proof now; if its only chart dependence is the old `IsThetaPaired` packaging, the right move is to port its actual contraction argument to the intrinsic arbitrary-cover equalizer, not invent a new hypothesis or a second descent theory.
